WHAT LEAVES THE STAKEHOLDER BOOK
- Chapter 10, Big ideas, all of it. These are funding tactics, and the owner deferred execution: "I want to nail the concept first and then execute" (2026-11-04T01:53Z).

- The Smoke card and every "Smoke is held". Smoke is held only in the render pipeline (2026-11-03T15:17Z); the owner never ruled on it.
- History: "second edition (draft)", "New in this edition", "The record", "Choose your weather" (a retired site section), the Tropos naming date with Atmosphere, and "predates the proposal".
- Process tags: proposal, target, placeholder, for review, to be drawn, to follow, still open.

STALE FACTS, each with a rewrite in the table
- Mantle "its light in the deck". That is an unsigned proposal; the light of the signed v3 is open (approved-renders.md:14-16). Commit 804cc8aa on origin/r47-brand already fixed this one line for the newer published version, 1794272741-39e1. Every other verdict applies to that version unchanged.

- "prices set at launch" becomes "price on request", tonight's site wording.

THE ONE QUESTION FOR THE OWNER (ask it on its own): should Planet EARF appear as where EARF is going?
- For: the bar, Mother EARF and EARFcoin are his own ideas, with his own design picks (README.md:126,131,135; "same with the bar", 2026-10-31T19:15Z).
- Against: naming the bar in public is his open call (FACTS.md:149), and he funded "$50K: prototypes + debut" over "$1.5M with the bar" (README.md:140).
- Until he says yes, these blocks are archived as internal.

items.text: 01 · Position / One material, cast in color, made to be heard and lit.
items.why: Chapter head; current.

items.text: What EARF is / Hi-fi and lighting in tinted cast acrylic, designed in San Francisco. Tropos, a powered horn loudspeaker, leads. Hemisphere and Core light the room in the same acrylic, and Mantle, a turntable, plays the records. Every piece comes in the same seven tints, so a room can be one color or three.
items.why: Matches the line as decided and the site preview (site RC index.html:1007-1018): powered horn speaker, two lamps, a turntable, seven tints.

items.text: For whom / People who arrange a room around listening and want the system to be the best-looking thing in it. Bars, hotels and restaurants that treat sound as part of the design, and need the room to look as good as it sounds. Collectors of design who would buy a speaker as an object first and discover it is a serious one.
items.why: Audience; "bars, hotels and restaurants" is the market, not Planet EARF.

items.text: Why now / Listening bars have spread from Tokyo to most large cities, and the habit has followed people home. Records came back to the living room. Interiors came back to color. And most high-end audio still arrives as a black box or a wood veneer. EARF answers them at once: color you can see through, a horn you can see into, light through the same material.
items.why: "came back" is market context, not EARF's own history.

items.text: What the brand holds to

items.text: The material is the message. Twenty millimeters of tinted acrylic carries light to its edges and shows what is inside. Nothing is painted on and nothing is hidden behind a veneer: the lining, the horn's driver, the amplifier's plate all show through the wall, so they are made to be seen.
items.why: Current: 20 mm walls, the lining, driver and amplifier plate show through (site RC index.html:988).

items.text: Color is a system, not a range. The seven tints are the same seven in every product and every application, always in the same order, always numbered. A customer chooses a color once and the whole catalog follows.
items.why: Current brand rule.

items.text: Engineering first, then the joke. The horn's profile and the cabinet's bass were simulated before any acrylic was cut, and the particulars are published to the millimeter. The wit lives in the names and the lines, never in the figures.
items.why: A method, stated as done work; matches the site ("worked out by simulation before any acrylic was cut", site RC index.html:967). Not a previous idea.
